topic: Science Process Skills: Observing Object Properties
key_concepts: Leaves can be described by their shape, color, and texture.
Leaf shapes include round, heart-shaped, long and thin, and long, narrow, and pointed.
Leaf texture can be smooth or rough.
Objects can be compared and arranged by size from smallest to largest.
Objects can be compared and arranged by weight from heaviest to lightest.
A balance can be used to compare the weight of two objects.
Adding an object to a bottle makes it heavier.
Objects have observable colors such as yellow, red, orange, green, and blue.
Objects have observable shapes such as round, rectangular, square, oval, and triangular.
Objects can be described as smooth or rough, and soft or hard.
An object can be described by its color, shape, texture, and hardness together.
Observation is a science process skill used to gather information using the senses.
